title: scikit-learn pipeline with mixed types and an unseen category
prompt_text:
scikit-learn 1.5 or later, pandas 2.x. Data:

```python
import pandas as pd
X = pd.DataFrame({
    "colour":   ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "blue", "green", "red", "blue"],
    "size_cm":  [10.0, 12.5, 9.0, 15.0, 11.0, 14.0, 10.5, 13.0],
    "weight_g": [120, 150, 110, 200, 140, 190, 125, 160],
})
y = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]
```

Build a single `Pipeline` that one-hot encodes `colour`, standardises the two numeric columns, and fits a `LogisticRegression`. Fit it on `X, y`. Then call `predict_proba` on this one-row frame, which contains a colour never seen in training, and it must not raise: `{"colour": "purple", "size_cm": 12.0, "weight_g": 150}`. Give the complete runnable code and explain in two sentences why the unseen colour does not cause an error. Do not use any library beyond pandas and scikit-learn.

Build a single `Pipeline` that one-hot encodes `colour`, standardises the two numeric columns, and fits a `LogisticRegression`. Fit it on `X, y`. Then call `predict_proba` on this one-row frame, which contains a colour never seen in training, and it must not raise: `{"colour": "purple", "size_cm": 12.0, "weight_g": 150}`. Give the complete runnable code and explain in two sentences why the unseen colour does not cause an error. Do not use any library beyond pandas and scikit-learn.

content:
```python
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# Define the data
X = pd.DataFrame({
    "colour":   ["red", "blue", "red", "green", "blue", "green", "red", "blue"],
    "size_cm":  [10.0, 12.5, 9.0, 15.0, 11.0, 14.0, 10.5, 13.0],
    "weight_g": [120, 150, 110, 200, 140, 190, 125, 160],
})
y = [0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1]

# Build the pipeline
numeric_features = ["size_cm", "weight_g"]
categorical_features = ["colour"]

preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(
    transformers=[
        ("num", StandardScaler(), numeric_features),
        ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'), categorical_features),
    ]
)

pipeline = Pipeline([
    ("preprocessor", preprocessor),
    ("classifier", LogisticRegression())
])

# Fit the pipeline
pipeline.fit(X, y)

# Predict on a row with an unseen colour
new_data = pd.DataFrame({"colour": ["purple"], "size_cm": [12.0], "weight_g": [150]})
proba = pipeline.predict_proba(new_data)
print(proba)
```

The unseen colour does not cause an error because the `OneHotEncoder` is configured with `handle_unknown='ignore'`, which means it silently ignores categories that were not present during training instead of raising a `ValueError`. This allows the encoder to produce zero-filled columns for unknown categories, enabling the downstream model to make predictions without crashing.
